To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

spammers tend to use the same set of registrars for registering domains, that they tend to re-use domains previously used by others, and finally, that they tend not to use the same registrar for both domain registration and hosting.

the registration behavior of spams is characterized by: 1) a small set of bulk registrars; 2) a small set and high frequency of domain name registrants; 3) a small number of domain name hosts; and 4) a small set (and high frequency) of domain name registrars.
spammers tend to register domains in bulk, that they tend to reuse domains, that they tend not to use privacy services, and that they register domains with only a few registrars.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the domain registration behavior that spammers exhibit.
the following question: can a registry or registrar detect the presence of a spammer during the domain registration process?

understanding the registration behavior of spammed domains and the characteristics of their registrars, with an eye toward developing techniques to identify malicious domains at the time of registration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spammers are not particularly clever, nor do they have a lot of imagination.
spammers do not register domains at random, and that they do not do so with the goal of evading blacklisting and takedowns.
spammers are lazy and they do not want to do things the right way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a way to identify spammers before they can even start spamming.
the domain registration behavior for spammers is not random.
the spammers have a very predictable behavior when it comes to domain registration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spammers' behavior can be observed at the domain registration stage and that this can be used to detect malicious domains before they become operational.
there is a significant amount of data that can be mined from the registration process to identify malicious activity.
there are features that can be used to distinguish between domains registered by spammers and those registered by legitimate users.
